arxiv-2411-09067.title: Dual-Space Invariance as a Definitive Signature of Critical States in Anderson Localization
arxiv-2411-09067.creator: Tong Liu
arxiv-2411-09067.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Tong Liu. Critical states represent a fundamental and fascinating research frontier in Anderson localization physics, known for their non-ergodic properties, including multifractal structure and self-similarity. However, exactly characterizing critical states continues to pose a significant challenge up to now. In this work, we establish a universal mechanism demonstrating that critical states must maintain dual-space invariance in both position and momentum representations, leading to delocalized dynamics in both spaces.

arxiv-2507-02592.title: WebSailor: Navigating Super-human Reasoning for Web Agent
arxiv-2507-02592.creator: Kuan Li, Zhongwang Zhang, Huifeng Yin, Liwen Zhang, Litu Ou, Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Baixuan Li, Zhengwei Tao, Xinyu Wang, Weizhou Shen, Junkai Zhang, Dingchu Zhang, Xixi Wu, Yong Jiang, Ming Yan, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang, Jingren Zhou[1em] Tongyi Lab , Alibaba Group
arxiv-2507-02592.description: Abstract Transcending human cognitive limitations represents a critical frontier in LLM training. Proprietary agentic systems like DeepResearch have demonstrated superhuman capabilities on extremely complex information-seeking benchmarks such as BrowseComp, a feat previously unattainable. We posit that their success hinges on a sophisticated reasoning pattern absent in open-source models: the ability to systematically reduce extreme uncertainty when navigating vast information landscapes.

arxiv-2508-10008.title: Multidimensional classification of posts for online course discussion forum curation
arxiv-2508-10008.creator: Antonio Leandro Martins Candido, José Everardo Bessa Maia
arxiv-2508-10008.description: Abstract The automatic curation of discussion forums in online courses requires constant updates, making frequent retraining of Large Language Models (LLMs) a resource-intensive process. To circumvent the need for costly fine-tuning, this paper proposes and evaluates the use of Bayesian fusion.

arxiv-2511-11867.title: Identifying Imaging Follow-Up in Radiology Reports: A Comparative Analysis of Traditional ML and LLM Approaches
arxiv-2511-11867.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have shown considerable promise in clinical natural language processing, yet few domain-specific datasets exist to rigorously evaluate their performance on radiology tasks. In this work, we introduce an annotated corpus of 6,393 radiology reports from 586 patients, each labeled for follow-up imaging status, to support the development and benchmarking of follow-up adherence detection systems.

arxiv-2601-13003.title: PrivFly: A Privacy-Preserving Self-Supervised Framework for Rare Attack Detection in IoFT
arxiv-2601-13003.creator: Safaa Menssouri, and El Mehdi Amhoud
arxiv-2601-13003.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Safaa Menssouri, and El Mehdi Amhoud. The Internet of Flying Things (IoFT) plays a vital role in modern applications such as aerial surveillance and smart mobility. However, it remains highly vulnerable to cyberattacks that threaten the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of sensitive data. Developing effective intrusion detection systems (IDS) for IoFT networks faces key challenges, including data imbalance, privacy concerns, and the limited capability of traditional models to detect rare but potentially damaging cyber threats.

pmc-11517947.description: BackgroundSystematic reviews are at the top of the evidence pyramid, but the whole process can be labor-intensive, especially in the screening by title and abstract of retrieved records. Large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, are proficient in natural language processing tasks and offer potential for accelerating this phase.

pmc-11657047.description: Silica nanoparticles (SNPs), one of the most widely researched materials in modern science, are now commonly exploited in surface coatings, biomedicine, catalysis, and engineering of novel self‐assembling materials. pmc-11728679.title: Digital Applications for Videoterminal-Associated Dry Eye Disease
pmc-11728679.creator: Maria Angela Romeo, Giulia Coco, Andrea Taloni, Giovanna Carnovale-Scalzo, Vincenzo Scorcia, Giuseppe Giannaccare
pmc-11728679.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Dry eye disease (DED) has become increasingly prevalent in the digital era, largely due to prolonged screen exposure. The excessive use of digital devices contributes to inappropriate blink frequency and dynamics, leading to ocular surface dryness and discomfort. Additionally, digital screen use has broader implications for systemic health, including visual strain, headaches, and disrupted circadian rhythms caused by blue light exposure.

pmc-11893324.title: Age tourism: going beyond health and “triple S” tourism toward a new request of journey
pmc-11893324.creator: Letizia Carrera
pmc-11893324.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). For many decades, the large part of developed countries has been experiencing the progressive ageing of their populations. This quantitative change is also accompanied by a qualitative shift in social representations of the third age. Within these changes, a fundamental role is played by the desire to experience opportunities for socializing, leisure, and culture that can shape a new and more complex concept of well-being. Within this context, tourism experience plays a crucial role.

pmc-12418920.description: One important property of any drug product is its stability over time. pmc-12525787.title: The Role of Anharmonicity in (Anti-)Ferroelectric Alkali Niobates
pmc-12525787.creator: Leif Carstensen, Wolfgang Donner
pmc-12525787.description: NaNbO3 (NN), known for the complexity of its phase transition sequence, is antiferroelectric (AFE) at room temperature, while both LiNbO3 (LN) and KNbO3 (KN) are ferroelectric (FE). The origin of ferroelectricity in ABO3 perovskites is believed to lie in the B-O hybridization, but the origin of antiferroelectricity remains unclear.

pmc-12547743.title: Single-Virus Lipid-Mixing Study of Sendai Virus Provides Insight into Fusion Mechanism
pmc-12547743.creator: Lisa Ji, Daniel Yuan, Abraham Park, Katherine Bai, Robert J. Rawle
pmc-12547743.description: Single-virus studies have proven useful to interrogate the entry mechanism for several viral families. Here, we employ a fluorescence microscopy-based single-virus assay to study the fusion (lipid mixing) of Sendai virus to model membranes, the first for any paramyxovirus to our knowledge. We find that fusion wait times following binding are exponentially distributed, suggesting a single rate-limiting step.

pmc-13417292.description: Porous ionic crystals (PICs) are porous molecular solids assembled through nondirectional Coulomb interactions, whose inherent structural flexibility during guest sorption and desorption creates adaptive pore environments that lead to unconventional gas sorption and separation selectivity.
